topic: Cell turnover: which body parts renew and which never do
hook: Your body rebuilds itself, except these parts

slides.title: Gut lining
slides.body: The cells lining your intestine are replaced every 3 to 5 days. They wear out fast from acid and digestion.
slides.image_prompt: Soft glowing pink folds of intestinal tissue with tiny finger-like villi, macro scientific illustration style, warm light

slides.title: Red blood cells
slides.body: Each one lives about 120 days before being recycled. Your bone marrow makes millions of new ones every second.
slides.image_prompt: Red disc-shaped blood cells flowing through a translucent vessel, deep red tones, macro 3D illustration

slides.title: Your skin's surface
slides.body: The outer layer of your skin renews roughly every 4 weeks, shedding tens of thousands of dead cells every minute.
slides.image_prompt: Extreme macro of skin surface texture with fine flakes lifting off, soft natural lighting, scientific style
slides.credit: Montavius Howard (TongCreator), from Pixabay (CC0) via wikimedia

slides.title: Your skeleton
slides.body: Bone is constantly broken down and rebuilt. Over about 10 years, your adult skeleton is almost fully renewed.
slides.image_prompt: Anatomical skeleton model standing against a dark background, dramatic side lighting, museum style

slides.title: Fat cells
slides.body: About 10% of your fat cells are replaced each year, but their total number stays almost fixed in adulthood, even after dieting.
slides.image_prompt: Round yellow fat cells packed together like bubbles under a microscope, soft scientific illustration

slides.title: Heart muscle
slides.body: Heart muscle cells renew under 1% per year at age 25, and even less later. Most stay with you for life.
slides.image_prompt: Realistic anatomical human heart model on a dark surface, red and purple tones, dramatic studio lighting

slides.title: Your eye lens
slides.body: The cells at the center of your eye lens formed before you were born. They are never replaced.
slides.image_prompt: Crystal clear glass lens glowing with soft light, floating on a dark background, symbolizing the eye lens

slides.title: Brain neurons
slides.body: Most neurons in your cerebral cortex are as old as you are. Carbon dating of brain cells proved it.
slides.image_prompt: Glowing network of neurons with branching connections in blue and violet light, dark background

cta: Follow for facts your body hides
caption:
You may have heard that your body replaces every cell every 7 years. It's not true. Your gut lining renews in days, but the center of your eye lens formed before you were born and is never replaced.

Scientists confirmed this by measuring carbon from 1950s nuclear tests, which acts as a hidden date stamp inside your cells.

Which one surprised you the most?
